newsitem.title: EAST TIMOR: Vatican creates new diocese in East Timor.
newsitem.headline: Vatican creates new diocese in East Timor.

text.p: Churchgoers in Indonesia's mostly Catholic East Timor were told on Sunday that a new diocese had been created in the former Portuguese colony, splitting the flock of Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo.

In a message read to parishioners in the local Tetum language, Indonesian and Portuguese, Belo said Pope John Paul II had chosen Monsignor Basilio Do Nascimento as the apostolic administrator of the new Baucau diocese covering the territory's eastern half.

Belo told parishioners of the new diocese, which includes the towns of Baucau, Los Palos and Viqueque, that Nascimento, a native East Timorese, would be consecrated in Rome on January 6 and before taking up his post in March.

"Now I will no longer be your shepherd. However, I am certain that God has chosen a shepherd who is good for you, a bishop who is clever and competent," Belo said in the message, also broadcast on local radio in East Timor.

"Please do not be unhappy. I will continue to say many prayers from Dili and together with your bishop I will make serious efforts to defend your human rights, to uphold peace and well-being in our territory," he said.

Belo, an immensely popular figure in the territory, was jointly awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize with self-exiled East Timorese independence advocate Jose Ramos Horta because of his long-standing record of defending his parishioners against human rights violations by the Indonesian military.
Last month, he again asserted his right to speak on the issue despite criticism from the Indonesian government over some of his comments.
Florentino Sarmento, a prominent member of the Catholic church's Commission for Justice and Peace in Dili, said Nascimento was a sociologist who had graduated from the Sorbonne in Paris.
He said Nascimento, who lived in Portugal for 27 years, returned to East Timor two years ago and had been long regarded as the favourite to head the new diocese.

"He is a very modest and reserved man but very much an intellectual," Sarmento told Reuters, adding Nascimento's "contextual" sermons were popular in Dili where he had served as Belo's assistant since his return.
He added that Nascimento, fluent in French and Portugese, had recently been studying Indonesian in the city of Yogyakarta.

Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 before declaring the territory its 27th province the following year, an act not recognised by the United Nations which still regards Portugal as the administering power.
